newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Rescue measures prescribed by the International Monetary Fund envisage tax reforms, the flotation of utility rates, higher value-added tax, strict controls on private sector debt creation and no help for finance and securities firms. IMF officials in Bangkok have also proposed growth be kept at four-five percent, inflation no more than seven percent and the current account deficit not more than five percent of gross domestic product. (BANGKOK POST)

- Finance officials have warned that Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is moving toward totalitarianism with a plan to set a "Super Status Body", which could bypass all ministries and agencies in implementing crucial economic policies. Prime Minister's Office Minister Bokhin Polakula, however, denies such a plan, saying Chavalit is too busy to assume absolute economic power, and that the current system already allowed him to intervene when needed. (THE NATION)

- Seen as a sign of the New Aspiration Party's control over government teachers, some 10,000 northeastern teachers continue their rally in Roi Et province for the second day yesterday in support of the Education Ministry's controversial supplementary funds. (THE NATION)

- Creditor banks of Alphatec Group are considering various ways of dealing with the financial crisis, including a takeover and converting debt into equity. Alphatec Group is currently faced with debts of over 30 billion baht. Its creditor banks are local and foreign financial institutions. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thailand's currency turmoil has put the oil industry in a financial crisis, with an aggregate loss of some 2.7 billion baht in the past month blamed on the baht's plunge. Five local oil refineries must have lost at least 1.7 billion baht due to higher payments for crude oil imports at the new exchange rate of about 32 baht to the U.S. dollar. (BANGKOK POST)
